claim_boundary: A scheduled FOMC policy statement can change discount-rate expectations and generate event-window uncertainty, but published primary evidence also reports muted or unstable Bitcoin responses. Exactly one future preregistered audit may test whether holding cash for the complete UTC day containing a regularly scheduled FOMC policy decision improves matched-capital BTC risk-adjusted economics. No causal, predictive or alpha claim is imported from the event calendar or literature.

feature_contract.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System

prior_matrix.identity: Federal Reserve FOMC meeting calendars and information
prior_matrix.finding: The official calendar states that the FOMC normally holds eight scheduled meetings per year and links each meeting to its policy statement and minutes. The 2021-2024 calendars identify the final decision date of each scheduled meeting before the event.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: A scheduled meeting date does not encode the direction or surprise content of monetary policy and does not establish that avoiding the entire UTC day is profitable.

prior_matrix.finding: The official history distinguishes the regular January, April, June, July, September, November and December meetings from unscheduled March meetings, notation votes and the cancelled March 17-18 meeting.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: Unscheduled and notation-vote events are excluded because they were not uniformly known at event-day 00:00 UTC; excluding them cannot later be reversed as a rescue.

prior_matrix.identity: Benigno and Rosa, The Bitcoin-Macro Disconnect, Federal Reserve Bank of New York Staff Report 1052
prior_matrix.finding: The paper studies high-frequency Bitcoin responses to macro and FOMC news and documents examples and broader evidence in which conventional assets respond while Bitcoin reactions are muted or unstable.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: High-frequency surprise regressions do not directly test full-day event risk, drawdown, transaction costs or a long-or-cash policy.

prior_matrix.identity: Kyriazis, Ofeidis, Palaiokrassas and Tassiulas, Monetary Policy, Digital Assets, and DeFi Activity
prior_matrix.finding: The event-study evidence reports negative crypto returns and greater volatility after unexpected U.S. monetary-policy tightening.
prior_matrix.transfer_boundary: The sign depends on the surprise, while the frozen calendar-only veto ignores statement direction and therefore must pass direct Design and Validation evidence.

future_design_requirements: Use only the final dates of regularly scheduled FOMC meetings in 2020-2024; exclude unscheduled meetings, notation votes, cancelled meetings, minutes releases, speeches, press conferences as separate events and post-event classifications.
Freeze and seal the exact official event-date list before accessing event-matched BTC outcomes; require 23 Design events in 2020-2022 and 16 Validation events in 2023-2024.
Measure complete-day return and intraday path drawdown from 00:00 UTC to the next 00:00 UTC; compare with non-event complete UTC days matched by event weekday in the same window.

Require event count, median return disadvantage, negative-rate difference, one-sided Fisher significance, path-drawdown disadvantage, annual breadth and top-event loss concentration in both Design and Validation before opening economics.

Only after every predictive gate passes, compare full-capital BTC with a zero-yield-cash event-day veto under matched capital, valuation, normal friction and doubled adverse friction. Require total return, maximum drawdown, Calmar, annual breadth, holding and terminal-inventory gates.

Do not add policy direction, surprise magnitude, SEP status, press-conference text, rate level, inflation, yield, equity, dollar, BTC trend, volatility, month, weekday, intraday-window, partial sizing, leverage or shorting variants.
Do not open post-2024 data; a historical pass remains REPORTED_NOT_ACTIVATED and requires separately sealed independent OOS.
uncertainty: The complete UTC day begins well before the usual FOMC statement and includes unrelated market moves; a full-day veto can lose positive pre-announcement drift.
A calendar-only feature mixes easing, tightening and no-change decisions and therefore may have volatility effects without a stable return direction.
The 2020 regular-meeting count is seven because the scheduled March meeting was cancelled; emergency March actions are deliberately excluded by the point-in-time rule.
Official historical pages prove event identity but not that every date was unchanged from its earliest tentative calendar publication; original calendar vintages remain MISSING_PROOF.
No FOMC-event-matched BTC return, path, strategy economics, post-2024 observation, candidate or OOS was accessed while freezing this prior.
